A fully unsupervised run earns trust by checking its output against tests or clear success criteria before calling the task done. You can also gate completion on relevant tests passing, so the run cannot mark the task finished until it has verified the result. [Source 2]

To keep a long session from drifting, use plan mode to scope non-trivial or risky work before changes begin, direct compaction by specifying what context to preserve, and use rewind to undo a wrong turn without discarding the rest of the session. Choose hands-on supervision for unfamiliar or high-stakes tasks, and goal-based autonomy for well-scoped, lower-risk work. [Source 1]
